Deterministically compiled from canonical evidence. Importance measures impact, not truth; evidence/confidence remain separate.

blocks.text: 1. Google DeepMind reports AI-assisted machine-checked proofs for selected Signal protocol code properties

Desk: evaluation_science Evidence: A · credible_unconfirmed · active · importance 6/10 (Major) Importance rationale: If the reported workflow generalizes, it could make machine-checked verification of high-impact software implementations more tractable and change how security assurance is produced. The evidence currently concerns one human-guided proof-of-concept, not verification of all Signal software or demonstrated scalable economics.

Demonstrated: The dated full paper and public Apache-2.0 proof repository were inspected. The existence and contents of the reported proof artifact are observable; proof validity, build reproducibility and theorem adequacy were not independently verified in this activation.

Claimed: The paper reports Lean-kernel-checked symbolic and computational security proofs for selected properties of compiled AArch64 libsignal CLI-harness code, and reports detection of two reintroduced historical bugs.

Mechanism: A human-guided specification agent and reviewer agents produce Lean theorem statements; autonomous prover agents generate proofs checked by Lean. The code is compiled to AArch64 and modeled with formal machine-code/Linux semantics. Hooked low-level cryptographic routines are represented by contracts.

Strongest baseline: Prior Signal formal verification and cryptographic-protocol proofs are discussed in the paper; WIRED reports this prior work provided a head start. No matched time/cost baseline was available.

Regime: Compiled AArch64 libsignal reference implementation in a CLI harness, selected one-to-one protocol sessions, fixed-length messages, no multi-device state, and explicit cryptographic, environment and attacker assumptions.

Open evidence gaps: The official repository is public, but its exact commit and dependencies were not pinned and the Lean proof build was not replayed in this activation.; No independent formal-methods review of the specifications, contracts, trusted computing base or proof coverage was inspected.; The inspected sources do not quantify compute, person-hours, expert review effort or matched cost versus earlier Signal verification work.

items: Anthropic revises its Usage Policy with explicit rules for deceptive campaigns and high-risk physical actions — importance 5/10 · Anthropic’s updated Usage Policy, marked effective November 12, 2026, adds explicit requirements for users connecting its models to hardware capable of high-risk physical actions: a qualified person must be able to observe and stop equipment, which must enter or hold a safe state if the person intervenes or service connectivity is lost. The revision also has a separate prohibition on deceptive campaigns and artificial activity, including fake personas, concealed sponsorship and networks of ostensibly independent sites. Comparison with Anthropic’s archived September 15, 2025 policy confirms the physical-action controls are new to this document. This is a provider usage policy, not a law; enforcement and resulting safety outcomes are unverified. — FCMO-E77F93F0C039

China and the African Union launch a joint mechanism for a 2026–2030 science partnership — importance 4/10 · China’s Ministry of Science and Technology and the African Union Commission held their first joint science-and-technology cooperation committee meeting in Wuhan on Nov 11, 2026. China’s minister said the committee would jointly implement the China–Africa Science and Technology Partnership Plan Enhancement Action for 2026–2030, including joint research and technology demonstrations. A separate ministry notice from the same forum says it released a report on typical AI application scenarios for African countries. The inspected official notices establish an announced cooperation mechanism and report release, not project funding, AI-specific implementation or outcomes. — FCMO-3853633AE4CD

ONS reports UK Q3 growth while leaving AI/cloud contribution unquantified — importance 4/10 · The ONS first estimate reports UK real GDP growth of 0.7% in 2026 Q3, with information and communication output up 2.1% and programming/consultancy up 4.4%. ONS says many of the businesses reporting the largest turnover increases are involved in AI- or cloud-related activities, but explicitly says the exact effect is difficult to quantify. This is not an AI-specific productivity estimate or causal GDP contribution; the first GDP estimate is preliminary. — FCMO-A2BEF9166DF6

Post-training theory identifies response-coverage collapse and a reference-reset remedy — importance 5/10 · A 141-page theory paper studies policy optimization for language-model post-training. It constructs a contextual-bandit setting where exact-gradient REINFORCE can lose probability mass on optimal responses even while reward rises, yielding exponentially slow convergence despite favorable initial response coverage. The authors introduce Approximate Policy Mirror Descent, which periodically resets the KL reference to the latest policy, and prove coverage-preserving convergence for stylized PPO/GRPO variants and squared-loss methods including Kimi-style objectives under stated assumptions. The main end-to-end guarantees rely on contextual-bandit and softmax-linear policies over frozen features; the paper does not show that deployed nonlinear LLM training runs exhibit the predicted collapse or gains. — FCMO-7FEEA30D5E7C
